title: United Airlines Plane Blows Tire During Takeoff at Chicago O'Hare, Passengers Deplane on Runway
excerpt: A United Airlines flight aborted takeoff at O'Hare International Airport after a tire blew during the takeoff roll, prompting an emergency response and forcing passengers to deplane on the runway.
body:
• A United Airlines plane blew a tire during takeoff at Chicago O'Hare International Airport on Wednesday, the FAA confirmed.
  • The flight aborted its takeoff and passengers were deplaned on the runway as emergency vehicles responded to the scene.
  • No injuries were reported. The FAA said it is investigating the incident.
  • The event is the latest in a string of tire-related incidents involving US airlines in recent months.

Emergency Response at O'Hare

A United Airlines flight blew a tire during takeoff at Chicago O'Hare International Airport on Wednesday, forcing the crew to abort the departure and triggering an emergency response on one of the nation's busiest runways.

https://x.com/WGNNews/status/2088013728188883172

The Federal Aviation Administration confirmed the incident, which occurred during the takeoff roll. Video from the scene showed emergency vehicles surrounding the aircraft on the runway as passengers were evacuated.

Passengers were deplaned directly on the runway using portable staircases before being bused to the terminal. No injuries were reported among passengers or crew members.

Pattern of Tire Incidents

The O'Hare incident adds to a growing list of tire-related events involving US airlines in 2026. Just a week earlier, a packed United Airlines flight bound for Los Cabos, Mexico, blew a tire during takeoff at San Francisco International Airport and returned safely with 165 passengers aboard.

In May, an American Airlines flight landed at O'Hare with two flat tires after arriving from Miami, leaving passengers stranded on the aircraft for about an hour before they could deplane. And in January, all rear landing tires on an international flight blew out upon landing at Atlanta's Hartsfield-Jackson Airport, causing damage inside the cabin.

Aviation experts have consistently said that tire failures, while alarming, are generally manageable safety events. Modern commercial aircraft are designed with redundant landing gear systems that allow safe operation even with damaged or missing tires.

FAA Investigation Underway

The FAA said it will investigate the cause of the blown tire. Such investigations typically examine maintenance records, tire age and wear, runway conditions, and whether the failure was caused by a manufacturing defect, maintenance issue, or foreign object debris on the runway.

United Airlines did not immediately provide details about the aircraft type involved or the flight's intended destination. The airline has faced heightened FAA scrutiny over its safety record in recent years, though the agency has not linked individual tire incidents to systemic maintenance problems.

O'Hare Under Pressure

The incident comes at a particularly busy time for O'Hare, which handles roughly 2,700 landings and takeoffs daily. The FAA recently extended flight capacity caps at the airport through October 2027, forcing United to cancel 10 planned new routes from its Chicago hub.

Chicago's airports have been the site of several high-profile aviation incidents in recent years. The FAA has maintained that individual mechanical events, while requiring investigation, do not necessarily indicate broader safety trends at the airport or with specific airlines.

Passengers whose flights were disrupted by Wednesday's incident were rebooked on later flights, the airline said.
